questions.q: In the query `SELECT Id, Case__r.Subject FROM Installation_Job__c`, what kind of relationship traversal is `Case__r.Subject`?
options: A parent-to-child subquery
A child-to-parent query using dot notation
An aggregate function
A SOSL search expression
questions.explain: Case__r.Subject walks up from the child Installation_Job__c to its parent Case using dot notation -- a child-to-parent relationship query.

questions.q: What is `Installation_Jobs__r` in a parent-to-child subquery from Case, per this lesson?
options: The API name of the Installation_Job__c object itself
A SOSL search clause
An aggregate function alias
The child relationship name, generated from the lookup field, used to query child records from the parent
questions.explain: The child relationship name is how you query child records from the parent object in a subquery, and it's generated from the lookup field -- distinct from, and easy to confuse with, the child object's own API name.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend the aggregate SOQL query (COUNT, SUM, GROUP BY) over pulling every Warranty_Claim__c record into Apex and summing it in a loop?
options: Aggregate queries are the only way to use the WHERE clause
Looping in Apex is not permitted on custom objects
It avoids risking the 50,000-row SOQL retrieval limit on a large data set and is simpler
SUM() cannot be used anywhere except in reports
questions.explain: Summarizing with GROUP BY and aggregate functions in the query itself avoids pulling potentially tens of thousands of records into Apex just to sum them, which risks the SOQL row-retrieval limit.

questions.q: Per this lesson's rule of thumb, when should you reach for SOSL instead of SOQL?
options: When searching loosely across text fields, possibly across multiple objects, without knowing in advance where the match is
Whenever querying a custom object instead of a standard object
When you know exactly which field and object to filter on
Only when writing Apex triggers, never in Flow
questions.explain: SOSL is for full-text search across one or more objects when you don't know in advance which object or field holds the match; SOQL is for filtering when you already know the object and field.

questions.q: What does "selectivity" mean for a SOQL query, per this lesson?
options: Whether the query selects more than one field
Whether the query uses GROUP BY
Whether the query is written in Apex rather than Flow
Whether the query's filters can use an index to narrow the result set efficiently
questions.explain: Selectivity is about whether a query's filter criteria rely on an indexed field (like a lookup, Id, or Name) to narrow results efficiently, rather than scanning non-indexed fields at scale.
